stem_text: An object of mass 'm' initially at rest on a smooth horizontal plane starts moving under the action of force F = 2N. In the process of its linear motion, the angle 𝜃 (as shown in figure) between the direction of force and horizontal varies as 𝜃=k𝑥 , where k is a constant and 𝑥 is the distance covered by the object from its initial position. The expression of kinetic energy of the object will be 𝐸=(𝑛)/(𝑘)sin⁡𝜃 . The value of n is ___________. [FIG-stem-1]

candidate_solve.derivation: Work done by variable force: W = int_0^x F_x dx' = int_0^x 2*cos(kx') dx' = (2/k)*sin(kx) = (2/k)*sin(theta). By Work-Energy Theorem, Delta K = E = W = (2/k)*sin(theta). Comparing with E = (n/k)*sin(theta) yields n = 2.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Work integral with position-dependent directional force F = 2N at angle theta = kx

representation_translation.evidence: Parameterizing horizontal force component Fx = F*cos(kx) and integrating along x

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Formulate W = int_0^x 2*cos(kx')dx', evaluate definite integral to (2/k)*sin(kx), equate to (n/k)*sin(theta)

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Direct calculus evaluation of cosine integral yielding coefficient n = 2

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Normal force and vertical component do no work on smooth horizontal plane

demand_proposal.rationale: Constructing dynamic work integral model with coupled variable angle force on frictionless plane
